metadata.title: AI Scaling Laws - Sources
metadata.description: Canonical papers and references for LLM scaling laws, compute-optimal training, Kaplan vs Chinchilla, and GPU compute estimation.

foundational_papers.name: Kaplan et al. — Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
foundational_papers.relevance: Original scaling laws paper (2020). Establishes power-law relationships between loss, model size (N), dataset size (D), and compute (C). Found N should scale faster than D — later corrected by Chinchilla. Primary reference for the pre-Chinchilla regime and the C ≈ 6ND approximation.

foundational_papers.name: Hoffmann et al. — Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models (Chinchilla)
foundational_papers.relevance: The Chinchilla paper (2022). Demonstrates that N and D should scale equally for a fixed compute budget, yielding the ~20 tokens-per-parameter heuristic. Provides the L(N,D) loss form and Table A3 with precise optimal (N*, D*) pairs. Required reading for any scaling law reasoning.

foundational_papers.name: Brown et al. — Language Models are Few-Shot Learners (GPT-3)
foundational_papers.relevance: GPT-3 paper (2020). 175B parameter model trained on ~300B tokens — a canonical example of a Kaplan-era under-trained model. Reference for GPT-3 sizing, training compute, and the few-shot emergence results that motivated scale-up.

foundational_papers.name: Radford et al. — Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners (GPT-2)
foundational_papers.relevance: GPT-2 paper (2019). 124M–1.5B parameter models; primary reference for GPT-2 architecture, training setup, and the 124M reproduction target. Token counts and architecture details are used in sizing worked examples.

extended_references.name: Goodfellow, Bengio, Courville — Deep Learning (textbook)
extended_references.relevance: Mathematical background for optimization, generalization, and capacity. Load just-in-time for foundational math (e.g., bias-variance tradeoff, regularization) when scaling law derivations require it.

extended_references.name: DeepMind Research Blog — Chinchilla Scaling Laws
extended_references.relevance: DeepMind's public blog post summarizing the Chinchilla result for practitioners. Good for quick orientation and the headline findings without the full paper.

extended_references.name: Epoch AI — Chinchilla's Wild Implications
extended_references.relevance: Epoch AI analysis (2022) of the practical implications of Chinchilla, including the data-constrained regime, over-training, and why most large models at the time were significantly undertrained. Useful for understanding the gap between Chinchilla-optimal and real-world deployments.

extended_references.name: Touvron et al. — LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
extended_references.relevance: LLaMA paper (2023). Early example of deliberate over-training past Chinchilla-optimal (7B params on 1T tokens) to produce inference-efficient models. Superseded by Llama 3 (15T tokens) for the extreme-over-training argument, but the original statement of the inference-cost rationale.

extended_references.name: Meta — Llama 3 Model Card
extended_references.relevance: Llama 3 (2024). 8B and 70B both trained on 15T tokens (~1,875 tok/param for 8B), ~75x Chinchilla-optimal. A canonical extreme-over-training datapoint (dense-model case; Llama 4 is the more current MoE example); performance improved log-linearly well past the Chinchilla point.

post_chinchilla_research.name: Besiroglu et al. — Chinchilla Scaling: A replication attempt
post_chinchilla_research.relevance: Epoch AI replication (2024) of Hoffmann et al. Approach 3. Shows the published parametric fit is biased (pre-convergence optimizer + rounding) with implausibly narrow confidence intervals; corrected exponents are alpha~0.35, beta~0.37. Mandatory caveat on any quote of the Chinchilla constants.

post_chinchilla_research.name: Muennighoff et al. — Scaling Data-Constrained Language Models
post_chinchilla_research.relevance: NeurIPS 2023. Up to ~4 epochs of repeated data are nearly as good as fresh data; marginal value decays to ~0 past ~16 epochs. Data-constrained generalization of Chinchilla; train smaller-for-more-epochs when data-bound.

post_chinchilla_research.name: Sardana & Frankle et al. — Beyond Chinchilla-Optimal: Accounting for Inference
post_chinchilla_research.relevance: ICML 2024. Adds inference cost to the scaling objective: deployed models should be smaller and trained far longer than Chinchilla-optimal. Quality improves out to ~10,000 tok/param. The rigorous basis for the over-training default.

post_chinchilla_research.name: Kumar et al. — Scaling Laws for Precision
post_chinchilla_research.relevance: 2024. Low-precision training reduces effective parameter count; post-training-quantization damage grows with training tokens, so over-training can harm a heavily-quantized deployment. Unifies training- and inference-precision effects. Relevant given FP8 training / INT4-8 serving in 2026.

post_chinchilla_research.name: Ludziejewski et al. — Scaling Laws for Fine-Grained Mixture of Experts
post_chinchilla_research.relevance: 2024. Introduces granularity (expert size vs FFN) as a scaling hyperparameter; G=1 (expert == dense FFN) is suboptimal at nearly every budget. Apply 6ND with activated params for MoE; granularity/sparsity are first-class knobs.

post_chinchilla_research.name: Pearce & Song — Reconciling Kaplan and Chinchilla Scaling Laws
post_chinchilla_research.relevance: 2024. Shows the Kaplan vs Chinchilla disagreement is methodological: parameter/FLOP counting at small scale, warmup duration, and scale-dependent optimizer tuning. Correcting these reproduces Chinchilla's N* ~ C^0.50 from Kaplan's setup.

post_chinchilla_research.name: Porian et al. — Resolving Discrepancies in Compute-Optimal Scaling of Language Models
post_chinchilla_research.relevance: NeurIPS 2024. Independent confirmation that the Kaplan/Chinchilla gap stems from last-layer compute, warmup, and optimizer tuning rather than a real disagreement about scaling behavior.

post_chinchilla_research.name: Snell et al. — Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
post_chinchilla_research.relevance: ICLR 2025. Test-time compute (sampling+verification, search) as a third scaling axis, substitutable with pretraining; the inference-to-pretraining token ratio sets the optimal split. Scaling law under the o1/o3 reasoning paradigm.

post_chinchilla_research.name: Busbridge et al. (Apple) — Distillation Scaling Laws
post_chinchilla_research.relevance: ICLR 2025. Law for distilled-student loss vs teacher/student compute allocation; compute-optimal distillation recipes for teacher-exists vs teacher-also-trained scenarios.

post_chinchilla_research.name: Wisconsin-Madison/Stanford — Test-Time Scaling Makes Overtraining Compute-Optimal
post_chinchilla_research.relevance: 2026. Train-to-Test (T2) scaling laws jointly optimizing model size, training tokens, and inference-sample count under one end-to-end train+inference budget; confirms planning for test-time sampling pushes optimal pretraining further into over-training. Verify against the latest revision before quoting fixed ratios -- most active scaling frontier in 2026.

post_chinchilla_research.name: Meta et al. — The Art of Scaling Reinforcement Learning Compute for LLMs
post_chinchilla_research.url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.13786 (UNVERIFIED -- confirm via arXiv search before use)
post_chinchilla_research.relevance: Oct 2025. First rigorous RL post-training compute scaling study (400K+ GPU-hours): RL compute-performance follows a sigmoidal curve with a recipe-dependent ceiling, not a clean Chinchilla-style power law. UNVERIFIED arXiv ID (not independently confirmed during the 2026-07-11 audit) -- search by title to find the current ID and figures before citing a specific number.

post_chinchilla_research.name: Scaling Behaviors of LLM Reinforcement Learning Post-Training
post_chinchilla_research.relevance: 2025. Finds RL post-training scaling saturates faster and differently than pretraining scaling; naive pretraining-style power-law extrapolation overstates expected RL-compute gains.

post_chinchilla_research.name: Meta — Llama 4 (Scout/Maverick/Behemoth) release materials
post_chinchilla_research.relevance: 2025. Current canonical over-training + MoE datapoint superseding Llama 3 for 'what's a current example': Scout/Maverick at 17B activated params (109B / ~400B total) trained on an estimated ~22-40T tokens; Behemoth (unreleased) targets ~288B activated / ~2T total params. Verify token/param figures against the live model card -- pre-release numbers were estimates.
